explain.label: Explain a concept with everyday examples
explain.prompt: Explain a concept to me using everyday examples: start with an intuitive analogy, then give the precise definition, and finish with the most common misconception. If I haven't said which concept, ask me first.

explain.label: Learn a topic from scratch
explain.prompt: I want to learn a topic from scratch. First tell me in three sentences what it is and why it matters, then walk me through the key ideas from simple to advanced. If I haven't named the topic or my background, ask me first — at most two questions.

explain.label: Compare two easily confused ideas
explain.prompt: Compare two ideas I keep mixing up: give each one's definition, the key differences and a typical example, then sum it up in a table. If I haven't said which two, ask me first.

explain.label: Check my understanding (Feynman method)
explain.prompt: Help me check whether I really understand a concept, Feynman-style: let me explain it in my own words first, then point out what I got wrong or left out, and follow up with one deeper question. If I haven't said which concept, ask me first.

solve.label: Walk me through a problem step by step
solve.prompt: Walk me through a problem one step at a time. For each step, give me a hint and let me try before showing the working — don't give away the final answer. If I haven't shared the problem yet, ask me to send it.

solve.label: Check my solution
solve.prompt: Check my solution to a problem: go through it step by step, find where and why it goes wrong, and give the corrected working in full. If I haven't shared the problem and my solution, ask me to send them.

solve.label: Sum up how to solve a type of problem
solve.prompt: Sum up the general approach to a type of problem: how to recognise it, the key steps, the usual traps, and one worked example. If I haven't said which type, ask me first.

solve.label: Solve one problem several ways
solve.prompt: Solve the same problem in at least two different ways, then compare the ideas behind them, when each one applies, and how much work each takes. If I haven't shared the problem yet, ask me to send it.

practice.label: Give me practice questions, easy to hard
practice.prompt: Give me 5 practice questions on one topic, from easy to hard. Show only the questions first; once I've answered, mark each one and explain. If I haven't said the topic and level, ask me first.

practice.label: Quiz me on what I'm learning
practice.prompt: Give me a quick quiz on what I've been learning: mix multiple-choice and short-answer questions, ask one at a time, and adjust the difficulty to my answers. If you're not sure what I've been learning, ask me first.

practice.label: Turn a mistake into practice
practice.prompt: I got a question wrong. First help me work out why, then write 3 variations on the same idea so I can practise it. If I haven't shared the question yet, ask me to send it.

practice.label: Make flashcards for a topic
practice.prompt: Turn a topic into 10 question-and-answer flashcards — a question on the front, a short answer on the back — good for spaced review. If I haven't said the topic, ask me first.

plan.label: Make a study plan
plan.prompt: Make me a study plan: weekly goals broken into small daily tasks, with review points marked. If I haven't said what I'm learning, for how long and how much time I have each day, ask me first — at most two questions.

plan.label: Map out a course or field
plan.prompt: Map out a course or field for me: the core modules, how they depend on each other, and the order I should learn them in. If I haven't said which one, ask me first.

plan.label: Plan my exam revision
plan.prompt: My exam is coming up. Plan a final review for me: rank the key points by importance, and set out what to review and how to test myself each day. If I haven't said the subject, what it covers and how many days are left, ask me first.

plan.label: Find my weak spots
plan.prompt: Ask me a few targeted questions to find my weak spots in a topic, then tell me what to shore up first. If I haven't said the topic, ask me first.

research.label: Get up to speed on a research field
research.prompt: Help me get up to speed on a research field: the problems it tries to solve, the main schools of thought and landmark work, where the frontier is now, and what to read first. If I haven't named the field, ask me first.

research.label: Read a paper closely with me
research.prompt: Read a paper closely with me: summarise the question, method and main findings, point out what's new and what's limited, and list the questions I should be able to answer afterwards. If I haven't shared the paper, ask me to send it or tell you its title.

research.label: Weigh both sides of a question
research.prompt: Lay out the main arguments and evidence on both sides of a question, the assumptions each side rests on, and then your overall judgement. If I haven't said what the question is, ask me first.

research.label: Outline a literature review
research.prompt: Draft an outline for a literature review on a topic: background, a framework for organising the work, the key points of each section, and the kinds of sources worth citing. If I haven't said the topic and what it's for, ask me first.
